# Container DNS surface area

Scope: name resolution inside a container on a user-defined network, whatever the network's driver.
This covers the `/etc/resolv.conf` that the daemon writes for the container and the embedded
DNS resolver behind it, as observable from outside the daemon.

This is a stub. It holds expectations that do not depend on any one driver. They come from the work
on the [Swarm networking surface area](swarm-networking.md) and from reviews of the specs' coverage. It is not yet a complete
account. [../README.md](../README.md) gives the model that this spec follows: the items of a
spec, their categories and what their verdicts depend on. [README.md](README.md) gives the
conventions of the networking specs, such as vantage points, daemon settings, timing and convergence
ceilings, and host requirements.

A container sends its DNS queries to the embedded DNS resolver, which is a DNS server that the
daemon runs for the container. The expectations state what the embedded resolver answers, and what
it forwards to upstream nameservers. A name resolves to an address when the embedded resolver
answers a DNS query for the name with that address. A container has external access when its default
route is on a network that is not `internal`, and replies to its egress traffic reach it. On a
bridge network with `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` set to `false`,
replies can fail to reach it ([Egress](bridge-networking.md#bridge-networking-egress)). The host's `resolv.conf` is
the `/etc/resolv.conf` that the daemon reads, even on a host that runs systemd-resolved.

On Linux nodes, the containers that follow do not use the embedded resolver, and nothing here
applies to them, other than the expectations whose state names the default bridge:

- A container attached only to the default bridge network.
- A container that uses the host's network.

<a id="container-dns-rationales"></a>

## Rationales

<a id="RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE**: Why a change to DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED should be deliberate

*Rationale of:* [DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED](#DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED)

It catches a change that makes the daemon rewrite a running container's /etc/resolv.conf after
the embedded resolver starts, such as removing 127.0.0.11 when the last user-defined network is
disconnected; the file is editable at runtime, and a rewrite would replace the user's edits, so
the change should be deliberate.

<a id="container-dns-host-requirements"></a>

## Host requirements

These requirements hold on Linux nodes. The conventions for this section are in [README.md](README.md#readme-host-requirements). The embedded resolver needs NAT rules in the container's network
namespace under the active firewall backend. It needs them whether or not the daemon's
**iptables** setting is true.

<a id="needextend-network-container-dns-5"></a>

<a id="container-dns-host-configuration"></a>

### Host configuration

<a id="DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS"></a>

**Host requirement DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS**: External access and host nameservers that resolve public names

*Platforms:* linux, windows · *Kind:* config

*Facility:* External network access, and nameservers in the host's `resolv.conf` that
resolve public names

*Needed when:* Always

<a id="container-dns-file-resolv-conf"></a>

## `resolv.conf`

This section holds on Linux nodes.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NAMESERVER**: The resolv.conf nameserver is 127.0.0.11

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The `/etc/resolv.conf` nameserver is `127.0.0.11`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-CTR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-CTR**: resolv.conf has the ndots from the container's DNS options

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose DNS options include a valid `ndots`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the `ndots` value from the container's DNS options.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST**: Without DNS options, resolv.conf has the host's ndots

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose DNS options are empty, and a host `resolv.conf` with a
valid `ndots`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the `ndots` value from the host's `resolv.conf`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-NO-HOST"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-NO-HOST**: With any container DNS option, resolv.conf has none of the host's

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose DNS options include any option

`/etc/resolv.conf` has none of the options in the host's `resolv.conf`,
`ndots` included.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO**: Without a valid ndots in effect, resolv.conf has options ndots:0

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose options in effect do not include a valid `ndots`

`/etc/resolv.conf` contains `options ndots:0`. This applies when the options
do not set `ndots`, and when all of the `ndots` values in them are
invalid.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-CTR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-CTR**: resolv.conf has the container's search domains

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container created with search domains

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the search domains that the container was created with.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DAEMON"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DAEMON**: Without its own search domains, resolv.conf has the daemon's dns-search

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container created without search domains, and a daemon with
`dns-search` set

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the daemon's `dns-search`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST**: Without any dns-search, resolv.conf has the host's search list

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container created without search domains, and a daemon without
`dns-search`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the search list from the host's `resolv.conf`.

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT**: A search domain of . is left out of resolv.conf

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`/etc/resolv.conf` does not contain a search domain of `.` given with
`--dns-search` or in the daemon's `dns-search`.

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT-ONLY**: With . as the only search domain, resolv.conf has no search line

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose only search domain, given with `--dns-search` or in
the daemon's `dns-search`, is `.`

`/etc/resolv.conf` does not have a `search` line, even if the host's
`resolv.conf` has one.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN**: Apart from ndots, resolv.conf lists the options as given

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Apart from `ndots`, `/etc/resolv.conf` lists the options in effect as they
were given.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-CTR-EDIT-KEPT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-CTR-EDIT-KEPT**: A process's change to resolv.conf is kept, across connects too

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container

After a process in the container changes the container's `/etc/resolv.conf`, the file
keeps the process's content. A connect or disconnect of the container does not change the file.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT**: After a connect from the default bridge, the container resolves names

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A host whose `/etc/resolv.conf` names a nameserver other than 127.0.0.53,
and a running container attached only to the default bridge whose `/etc/resolv.conf` has
not changed since the daemon wrote it

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to a user-defined network responds 200, the
container resolves the names of the containers on that network. It resolves other names through
the nameservers in the host's `resolv.conf`, loopback nameservers included. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER**: After a connect from the default bridge, the nameserver is 127.0.0.11

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container attached only to the default bridge, whose
`/etc/resolv.conf` has not changed since the daemon wrote it

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to a user-defined network responds 200, the
`/etc/resolv.conf` nameserver is `127.0.0.11`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-USER-DEFINED-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-USER-DEFINED-START**: A container started on a user-defined network keeps its resolv.conf

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that started with an endpoint on a user-defined network

The container's `/etc/resolv.conf` keeps the content that it had at start. This holds
after later connects and disconnects.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-AFTER-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-AFTER-CONNECT**: After a connect from the default bridge, resolv.conf stops changing

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that started attached only to the default bridge, and that a
later connect attached to a user-defined network

The container's `/etc/resolv.conf` keeps the content that it had after that connect. This
holds after later connects and disconnects.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-RESOLVER-AFTER-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-RESOLVER-AFTER-DISCONNECT**: The embedded resolver keeps answering after the last disconnect

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that has had an endpoint on a user-defined network at any time
since it started

After the container disconnects from every user-defined network, the embedded resolver continues
to answer the container's queries. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

A container's DNS options are the options that it was created with. If it was created without DNS
options, they are the daemon's `dns-opts`. The options in effect are the container's
DNS options when it has any. Otherwise, they are the options in the host's `resolv.conf`. A
valid `ndots` is an integer of 0 or more. `/etc/resolv.conf` keeps a valid
`ndots` above 15 as given, although glibc treats any `ndots` above 15 as 15.

<a id="container-dns-names-and-answers"></a>

## Names and answers

In this section, the querying container is the container that sends the DNS query. The embedded
resolver has records for a name on a network when an endpoint on that network has that name. An
endpoint's names are its container's name, short ID and hostname, and its network aliases. In
`<name>.<network>`, `<name>` stands for a name and `<network>` for the name of a
network. Both are placeholders, not literal text.

An expectation in this section names `none` when the embedded DNS resolver answers the query from
its own records. It does this the same way on every platform.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME**: A container's name resolves to its address on a shared network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A container's name resolves to its address on a network it shares with the querying container.
See [Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-CASE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-CASE**: Names and aliases resolve whatever the case of the query

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A container's name and its network aliases resolve whatever the case of the query: a container
named `Web` resolves as `web` and as `WEB`.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ALIAS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ALIAS**: A network alias resolves on its network only

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A network alias given to a container's endpoint resolves to the container's address on that
network, for containers on that network only.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED**: An alias that several containers share resolves to all of them

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Several containers on a network whose endpoints have the same network alias, where

The alias resolves to the addresses of all of those containers on that network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME**: A container's short ID and hostname resolve as its name does

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A container's short ID (the first 12 hex digits of its ID) and its hostname resolve as its name
does.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES**: DNSNames lists the name and then the aliases, which all resolve

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container on a user-defined network

`GET /containers/{id}/json` lists in
`NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.DNSNames` the container's name, and then the
aliases of its endpoint on that network. The name and each alias resolve on that network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-SHORT-ID"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-SHORT-ID**: DNSNames lists the short ID and the hostname after the aliases

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container on a user-defined network

`NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json`
lists the container's short ID and then its hostname after the aliases. It does not list a name
more than once.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME**: After a rename, DNSNames has the new name and not the old one

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container whose hostname is not its name

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container responds 204,
`NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json`
has the new name for each user-defined network. It does not have the old name. Its other entries
do not change.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: DNSNames on the default bridge is empty

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container attached to the default bridge

`NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json` is
empty.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME**: After a rename, DNSNames on the default bridge lists the new names

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container attached to the default bridge

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container responds 204,
`NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames` lists the new name, the short ID and, when
it differs from the short ID, the hostname. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK**: A name resolves if it exists on any of the querying container's networks

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A name resolves when an endpoint with that name exists on any network that the querying
container is attached to.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-OTHER-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-OTHER-NETWORK**: A query gets no address from a network the querying container is not on

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A query for a name does not get the address of an endpoint on a network that the querying
container is not attached to.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-START**: After a start, a container's name and aliases resolve on its networks

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped standalone container

After `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 204, its name and its
aliases on each of its networks resolve for the other containers on that network. This holds
whether or not the container has a healthcheck.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-CONNECT**: After a connect, a container's name and aliases resolve on the network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running standalone container

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container responds 200, its name and its
aliases on that network resolve for the other containers on the network. This holds whether or
not the container has a healthcheck.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DISCONNECT**: After a disconnect, a container's name and aliases stop resolving there

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a user-defined network

After `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container from that network responds 200,
the other containers on that network do not resolve its name or aliases to its address on that
network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-STOP"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-STOP**: After a stop, a container's name and aliases stop resolving

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with endpoints on user-defined networks

After `POST /containers/{id}/stop` for the container responds 204, the other containers
on each of those networks do not resolve its name or aliases to its address on that network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-RENAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-RENAME**: After a rename, the new name resolves and the old one does not

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, and a running container whose hostname is not its
name

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container responds 204, its new name
resolves and its old name does not, for containers on each of its networks.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM**: In a Swarm, a rename applies on a multi-host network on its own node

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A node in a Swarm, and a running container whose hostname is not its name, with an
endpoint on a Swarm-scoped network of a multi-host driver, such as `overlay`

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container responds 204, its new name
resolves and its old name does not, for containers on that network on its node. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals). [*SWARM-SD-RENAME*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-RENAME) covers containers on
other nodes.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS**: A and AAAA queries for a known name are answered from its records

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver answers an A or AAAA query for a name that it has records for from those
records. This holds for a single-label name too, whatever `ndots` the options in
effect set ([resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf)).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-AAAA"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-AAAA**: An AAAA query returns the container's IPv6 address on a shared network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container on a network with IPv6 that it shares with the querying container,
other than an overlay network, where no other network of the querying container has an endpoint
with that container's name

An AAAA query for that name returns the container's IPv6 address on the shared network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING**: A query of the address type a name lacks gets an empty NOERROR

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Records in the embedded resolver for a name that are all A records, or all AAAA
records

A query of the other type for that name gets an empty `NOERROR` response. The embedded
resolver does not forward this query upstream.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-MX"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-MX**: An MX query for a known name gets an empty NOERROR response

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

An MX query for a name that the embedded resolver has A or AAAA records for gets an empty
`NOERROR` response. The embedded resolver does not forward this query upstream.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPE-FORWARDED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPE-FORWARDED**: Queries of types other than A, AAAA, MX, PTR and SRV are forwarded

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver forwards upstream a query of a type other than A, AAAA, MX, PTR and SRV.
This holds for a name that it has records for too.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER**: Outside a Swarm, A and AAAA answers come from the first network only

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux node that is not in a Swarm

Several of the querying container's networks can have records for a name. The embedded resolver
answers an A or AAAA query for that name from the records of the first network only. The order
is: (1) Endpoints with a higher `GwPriority` first. (2) Networks that are not
`internal` first. (3) Endpoints with a gateway or default route for more IP versions first.
(4) Network names in byte order. When that network does not have an address of the family asked
for, the query gets an empty `NOERROR` response. This holds even if another network has
one.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE**: Answers list all addresses unless the UDP size limit truncates them

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Over UDP, an answer from the embedded resolver's own records lists all of the name's addresses
when it fits in a size limit. The limit is the larger of 512 bytes and the query's EDNS0 buffer
size. When the answer does not fit, the embedded resolver truncates it and sets the TC bit. Over
TCP, the answer lists all of the name's addresses.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER**: The order of a name's addresses varies from one answer to the next

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

In answers from the embedded resolver's own records, the order of a name's addresses varies from
one query to the next.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-TTL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-TTL**: Answers from the embedded resolver's records have a TTL of 600 seconds

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The records in an answer from the embedded resolver's own records have a TTL of 600 seconds.
This holds for A, AAAA and PTR answers.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-PTR**: Reverse lookups resolve the addresses of containers on shared networks

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Reverse (PTR) lookups resolve for the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of containers on the querying
container's networks.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP**: A forward lookup of a reverse lookup's answer returns the address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A forward lookup of the name that a reverse lookup returns for a container's address returns
that address.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM**: A reverse lookup answers <name>.<network>. with the container name

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The answer to a reverse lookup of a container's address is `<name>.<network>.`, where
`<name>` is the container's name and `<network>` is the network's name. It is never an
alias, the short ID or the hostname.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED**: <name>.<network> resolves to the addresses of <name> on that network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A querying container attached to the network `<network>`, and records for
`<name>` on that network

A query for `<name>.<network>` resolves to the addresses of `<name>` on that network
only. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE**: In <name>.<network>, the network part matches only in the same case

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

In a `<name>.<network>` query, `<network>` matches a network only when its case is
the same as the case of the network's name. `<name>` matches whatever its case.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED**: <name>.<network> is forwarded when the querying container is not on it

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network whose name is a valid DNS label and that the querying container is not
attached to, where no network of the querying container has an endpoint named
`<name>.<network>`, `<network>` being that network's name

The embedded resolver forwards a query for `<name>.<network>` upstream.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME**: An endpoint named <name>.<network> wins over <name> on <network>

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A querying container attached to the network `<network>`, where an endpoint is
named `<name>`, and an endpoint named `<name>.<network>` on one of the querying
container's networks

`<name>.<network>` resolves to the address of the endpoint with the whole name. It
does not resolve to the address of `<name>` on the network `<network>`.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS**: A link alias resolves to the linked container for the linking one only

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with `<name>:<alias>` in the `Links` of
its endpoint settings for a user-defined network

The alias resolves to the named container's address on that network. It resolves only for
queries from the container that has the link.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE**: A link alias takes precedence over names on the container's networks

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

An alias in the `Links` of any of the querying container's endpoints takes precedence
over the names and network aliases on the container's networks. The alias resolves to the linked
container even when another container on one of those networks has that name.

<a id="container-dns-forwarding"></a>

## Forwarding

<a id="DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES**: Public DNS names resolve

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container that has external access

Public DNS names resolve.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL**: An internal-only container never queries unreachable or host nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container attached only to `internal` networks

The embedded resolver does not forward the container's queries to any nameserver that the
container cannot reach from its own network namespace. It also does not forward them to the
nameservers in the host's `resolv.conf`.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL**: Unknown names get SERVFAIL in an internal-only container without --dns

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container attached only to `internal` networks and created
without `--dns` nameservers, whose daemon does not have a `dns` setting

A query for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for gets SERVFAIL. When the
options in effect set `ndots`, a single-label A or AAAA query gets an empty
`NOERROR` response instead ([resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf),
[*DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL*](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)).

<a id="DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS**: The embedded resolver forwards to the --dns nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container that has external access and was created with `--dns`
nameservers

The embedded resolver forwards to the nameservers set with `--dns`, in place of the
host's nameservers.

<a id="DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS**: Without --dns, the embedded resolver forwards to the daemon's dns

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Applies to:* A daemon with a `dns` setting, and a container that has external
access and was created without `--dns` nameservers

The embedded resolver forwards to the nameservers in the daemon's `dns` setting, in
place of the host's nameservers.

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER**: An internal-only container resolves through a --dns nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

networks

The container created with `--dns` resolves names through that nameserver.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER**: An internal-only container resolves through the daemon's dns nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

The container created without `--dns` nameservers resolves names through that

<a id="DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS**: Without dns settings, the host's nameservers are queried from the host

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container that started with an endpoint on a user-defined
network, has external access and was created without `--dns` nameservers, whose daemon
does not have a `dns` setting

The embedded resolver forwards to the nameservers in the host's `resolv.conf`, loopback
nameservers included. It queries them from the host's network namespace.

<a id="DNS-FWD-CONFIGURED-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-CONFIGURED-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS**: Configured nameservers are queried from the container's namespace

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver queries nameservers set with `--dns` or in the daemon's
`dns` setting from the container's network namespace.

<a id="DNS-FWD-FAILOVER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-FAILOVER**: No response, SERVFAIL or REFUSED moves the query to the next nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver forwards a query to the next nameserver when the current nameserver does
not respond, or responds SERVFAIL or REFUSED. When each nameserver that it forwards to does not
respond, or responds SERVFAIL or REFUSED, the client gets SERVFAIL.

<a id="DNS-FWD-FAILOVER-TIMEOUT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-FAILOVER-TIMEOUT**: Over UDP, SERVFAIL comes within 4 seconds per unresponsive nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Over UDP, when no nameserver that the embedded resolver forwards a query to responds, the client
gets SERVFAIL within 4 seconds times the number of those nameservers.

<a id="DNS-FWD-RESPONSE-RETURNED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-RESPONSE-RETURNED**: Any other nameserver response, NXDOMAIN included, goes to the client

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver returns a nameserver's response other than SERVFAIL or REFUSED, NXDOMAIN
included, to the client. It does not ask the next nameserver.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-LIMIT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-LIMIT**: The embedded resolver forwards to at most the first three nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver forwards to at most the first three nameservers.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF**: A configured nameserver 127.0.0.11 is skipped and not counted

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver does not forward to a nameserver `127.0.0.11` set with `--dns`
or in the daemon's `dns` setting. That nameserver does not count toward the three
nameservers.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY**: With 127.0.0.11 as the only nameserver, unknown names get SERVFAIL

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container whose only nameserver, set with `--dns` or
in the daemon's `dns` setting, is `127.0.0.11`

A query for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for gets SERVFAIL. When the
options in effect set `ndots`, a single-label A or AAAA query gets an empty
`NOERROR` response instead ([resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf),
[*DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL*](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)).

<a id="DNS-FWD-MULTI-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-MULTI-LABEL**: An unknown multi-label A or AAAA query is forwarded upstream

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The embedded resolver forwards upstream an A or AAAA query for a multi-label name that does not
match any container, service or alias on the querying container's networks. This does not hold
for `<name>.<network>` when the querying container is attached to a network named
`<network>` and the embedded resolver has records for `<name>` on it
([*DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED*](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED)).

<a id="DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL**: An unknown single-label name is forwarded on Windows or without ndots

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container on a Windows node, or a container on a Linux node whose options in
effect, per [resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf), do not set `ndots`

The embedded resolver forwards a single-label A or AAAA query upstream when it does not have a
record for the name.

<a id="DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS**: With ndots of 1 or more, an unknown single-label name gets empty NOERROR

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container on a Linux node whose options in effect, per
[resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf), set `ndots` to 1 or more

A single-label A or AAAA query gets an empty `NOERROR` response when the embedded
resolver does not have a record for the name. The embedded resolver does not forward the query
upstream. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

The expectation for an `ndots` of 1 or more is a detector because the behavior itself is
in question. [moby/moby#53157](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/53157) proposes to put
container names in a domain on the search list. That change would make this behavior unnecessary. An
`ndots` of 0, or an invalid `ndots`, has the same effect. That effect is a
bug for these values. See [Known divergences & non-goals](#container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="container-dns-port-53-in-the-container"></a>

## Port 53 in the container

This section holds on Linux nodes.

<a id="DNS-PORT53-BIND"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-PORT53-BIND**: A process binds port 53 on 127.0.0.11 without error and gets no packets

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A process in the container can bind UDP and TCP port 53 on `127.0.0.11` without an error. No
packet reaches that socket.

<a id="DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES**: Without the iptables command, queries to 127.0.0.11 get no answer

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [BR-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with the iptables backend and **iptables** false, on a host
without the **iptables** command, and a running container with an endpoint on a
user-defined network

A DNS query from the container to `127.0.0.11` does not get an answer. See [Host
requirements](#container-dns-host-requirements).

<a id="DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES-LOG"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES-LOG**: Without the iptables command, the daemon logs the DNAT/SNAT failure

*Observed from:* log · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [BR-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with the iptables backend and **iptables** false, on a host
without the **iptables** command, and a running container with an endpoint on a
user-defined network

The daemon log contains `setting up DNAT/SNAT rules failed`. See [Host requirements](#container-dns-host-requirements).

<a id="container-dns-known-divergences-non-goals"></a>

## Known divergences & non-goals

<a id="DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL**: Single-label forwarding with an ndots of 0 or an invalid ndots

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Not forwarded. This applies when the options in effect set `ndots` to 0 or to an
invalid value. A single-label A or AAAA query then gets an empty `NOERROR` response when
the embedded resolver does not have a record for the name. This is the same as for an
`ndots` of 1 or more ([Forwarding](#container-dns-forwarding)). Only an `ndots`
of 1 or more is meant to have that effect ([moby/moby#53104](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/53104)). The effect shows in Docker-in-Docker. The inner
daemon reads the outer container's `resolv.conf` as the `resolv.conf` of its host.
The inner daemon finds the `ndots:0` that the outer daemon added. The containers of
the inner daemon cannot resolve names that only the outer resolver knows.

<a id="DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL**: Single-label queries after a live restore

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Forwarded. After the daemon restarts with `live-restore` true, the embedded
resolver forwards upstream a single-label A or AAAA query that it does not have a record for,
from a container that kept running. This occurs whatever `ndots` the options in
effect set ([Forwarding](#container-dns-forwarding)).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE**: Renaming a container on a Swarm node

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Not applied. On a node in a Swarm, `POST /containers/{id}/rename` changes the
container's records only on Swarm-scoped networks of multi-host drivers, such as `overlay`. It
does not change them on other networks, such as user-defined bridge networks and Swarm-scoped
networks of node-local drivers. The container's new name does not resolve there. Its old name
continues to resolve there after the rename. The old name continues to resolve there after the
container is removed ([Names and answers](#container-dns-names-and-answers)).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS**: Records after a node leaves a Swarm

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Lost. Take a node in a Swarm, whether it created the Swarm with `POST /swarm/init` or
joined it, that leaves it with `POST /swarm/leave`. After the leave, the names of the
containers that were running on the node's user-defined networks before the leave stop resolving
there. A container that starts after the leave gets records that resolve
([Names and answers](#container-dns-names-and-answers)).

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED**: resolv.conf after the embedded resolver starts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* Why a change to DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED should be deliberate ([RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE](#RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE))

Not updated. After the embedded resolver starts for a container, `/etc/resolv.conf` does
not change again while the container runs. A container that disconnects from every user-defined
network keeps `nameserver 127.0.0.11` and the embedded resolver. A container started
on the default bridge alone gets the host's nameservers ([resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf)).

<a id="DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM**: Upstream nameservers after a connect from the default bridge

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

On a Linux node whose `/etc/resolv.conf` names only 127.0.0.53, take a container that
started attached only to the default bridge and later connects to a user-defined network. It
forwards to the nameservers in `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf`, not to 127.0.0.53
([resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf), [Forwarding](#container-dns-forwarding)).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED**: DNSNames on the default bridge after a rename

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Filled in. On Linux nodes, `GET /containers/{id}/json` does not report
`DNSNames` for the default bridge, which does not have name resolution. After a
rename of the running container, it reports the new name, the short ID and the hostname there.
These names do not resolve for a container attached to the default bridge alone. On a node that
is not in a Swarm, a container attached to the default bridge and a user-defined network
resolves the new name and the short ID to the renamed container's address on the default bridge
([Names and answers](#container-dns-names-and-answers)).

<a id="DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-PTR-ROUND-TRIP"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-PTR-ROUND-TRIP**: Reverse-lookup round trip on Windows

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

Fails. A reverse lookup returns `<name>.<network>`. The embedded resolver on a Windows
node does not answer names in that form. It forwards a query for such a name upstream
([Names and answers](#container-dns-names-and-answers)).

<a id="DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS**: Nameservers on internal networks on Windows

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

Not applied. A Windows endpoint on an `internal` network does not get the nameservers set with
`--dns` or in the daemon's `dns` setting. A Windows container attached
only to `internal` networks cannot resolve names through a nameserver on one of them
([Forwarding](#container-dns-forwarding)).

<a id="container-dns-deliberately-not-asserted"></a>

## Deliberately not asserted

- The comments the daemon writes into `resolv.conf`, such as its header and its record of
  where `ndots` came from.
- The ports that the embedded resolver listens on.
- The firewall rules that the daemon programs in a container's network namespace: whether they
  exist, their content and names, and the hooks and priorities of their base chains.
